objective: Prove: (1) every closed sphere of the two-kind law (co-lines of two or three points) has six digons, and with the local Kasteleyn sign rule carries the knot's contradiction; (2) a law of radius r without hidden states that has the octahedral sphere K_m (m >= 2r + 1) also has every capped tube T(m, L, tau) with L >= 2r + 1, whose contradiction has resolution width O(m) at every length; (3) the seam law (one hidden bit per incidence: all four incidences of a digon are seams, a co-line of three points has none or one opposite pair) has exactly the K_m as its closed spheres, each with one marking, so it grows round spheres at every size whose contradiction has width Theta(sqrt n) and size 2^Theta(sqrt n); (4) a law without branching grows at most one closed surface. Check on octahedral spheres, tubes of every twist and random grown spheres, with controls.
status: Proved 2026-11-07: every closed two-kind sphere has six digons and, with local Kasteleyn signs, a contradiction; a law of radius r without hidden states that allows K_m (m >= 2r + 1) allows every capped tube, whose contradiction has resolution width O(m) at every length; the seam law (one hidden bit per incidence, two rules at co-lines) has exactly the octahedral knot spheres K_m as its spheres, each with one marking, so all its contradictions need width Theta(sqrt n) and size 2^Theta(sqrt n); a growth law without branching grows at most one closed surface.
title: Round spheres need one hidden bit per incidence
